This section will go through assessing temperature research through GEE.

## Summary

### Land Surface Temperature

Land Surface Temperature (LST) is a parameter that reflects land-atmosphere interactions from regional to global scales as well as an indicator that influences the rate and timing of vegetation growth [@li2023a].

Try to look at different LST mapping under different climates.

Bangkok Thailand is characterise by a hot humid rainy climate

::: {layout-ncol="2"}
![Landsat LST](images/w9_images/before_QA_PIXEL.png)

![MODIS, Aqua and Terra](images/w9_images/MODIS_LST.png)
:::

Astonia, USA is characterised by an extremely hot dessert climate.

::: {layout-ncol="2"}
![Landsat LST](images/w9_images/LANDSAT_LST.png)

![MODIS, Aqua and Terra](images/w9_images/MODIS.png)
:::

![LST Chart](images/w9_images/LST_CHART.png)

![Average Temperature Comparison Across Time (Maricopa and Pima)](images/w9_images/compare.png)

Looking at the chart it shows that the minimum temperature between the time series is a bit over 30 as a minimum and max temperature exceeding 50. Therefore, try changing minimum maximum temperature below,

::: {layout-ncol="2"}
![Level 2 minimum 30 maximum 60](images/w9_images/level2.png){alt="Landsat LST"}

![Level 2 with minimum 20 maximum 50](images/w9_images/level1_zoom.png){alt="MODIS, Aqua and Terra"}
:::

GEE code for this practical can be found [here](https://code.earthengine.google.com/0c9f8558f28a429a32895861098c6ecb).

+-----------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Strengths | Limitations                                                                                                     |
+===========+=================================================================================================================+
|           | -   Highly depends on atmospheric correction (Cloud coverage can affect accuracy, see Reflection section below) |
|           |                                                                                                                 |
|           | -   Difficult to separate surface temperature, surface emissivity and atmospheric effects                       |
|           |                                                                                                                 |
|           | -   Represents radiometric temperature (surface) not physical temperature                                       |
|           |                                                                                                                 |
|           | -   Mixed pixels makes it harder to interpret over heterogeneous surfaces                                       |
|           |                                                                                                                 |
|           | -   Surface temperature changes quickly and varies across different times of the day, making validation harder  |
|           |                                                                                                                 |
|           |     (Validation methods: T-based / R-based / Intercomparison Method / Bibliometric Analysis)                    |
+-----------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

: Sources: @li2013, @li2023a

## Applications

### LST Products

| Resolution | Products | Typical Spatial Resolution |
|----|----|----|
| Low | ASTER, Landsat | 90 m, 30 m |
| Medium | MODIS, with EOS/Aqua and Terra | 1 km |
| High | LSA-SAF (MSG/SEVIRI), GOES-R ABI, Copernicus Global Land Service / GlobTemperature | 3–5 km, 2–10 km, 0.05° |

: Sources: @li2023a
